newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay calls Mercosur meeting on Brazil rules.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay calls Mercosur meeting on Brazil rules.

text.p: Paraguay Thursday called an urgent meeting of the finance ministers and central bank presidents of the Mercosur customs union to discuss moves by Brazil to cut down on its imports.

"We have informed (Brazil's Finance Minister) Pedro Malan that, after reaching an agreement with Argentina, we have called a meeting of economy ministers and central bank presidents for April 23," Paraguay's Finance Minister Miguel Maidana told a news conference.

Maidana will meet Malan in Brasilia next Wednesday to present the Paraguayan case against Brazil's decision in late March to slap new limits on import financing for less than 360 days, effectively forcing importers to pay cash.
After howls of protest by its Mercosur partners, Brazil agreed to water down the new rules for Mercosur countries for 120 days while a permanent solution was sought.
Mercosur groups Brazil with Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. Chile is an associate member with a free-trade agreement but does not participate in the customs union.
About half of Paraguay's total 1996 exports of $1.1 billion went to Brazil.
